subject: EastUS3: Graceful warm-restart maintenance window (Aug 25, 2026)
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: customers-eastus3@redwood-notify.com, Jacqueline Hart <jacqueline.hart@acme-cloud.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: EastUS3: Graceful warm-restart maintenance window (Aug 25, 2026)

Hello EastUS3 customers —

We are scheduling a planned, low-impact maintenance window for the EastUS3 region on Tuesday, Aug 25, 2026 between 01:00–05:00 UTC. This work is a coordinated warm-restart of driver stacks and a small kernel refresh to address stability regressions observed at high sequence lengths.

What to expect:
- Rolling warm-restarts across host pools; we will avoid full instance replacements.
- Typical per-request latency should remain within SLOs; a small percentage of long-running streams may see reconnects.
- Automatic workload rebalancing; we will prioritize pinned dedicated pools last to reduce disruption.

Action for customers:
- No action required for most workloads.
- If you have long-lived streaming sessions or heavy KV-cache usage, please plan for brief reconnects.
- If you need an exception (e.g., fixed tenancy that cannot tolerate restarts), reply to this thread by EOD Friday Aug 21 with your tenancy IDs.

Attachments: eastus3-warm-restart-runbook.pdf (overview, rollback steps), eastus3-maintenance-window.csv (detailed host-pool schedule)

We will post live updates on the status page and provide a post-maintenance summary.

Thanks —
Vanessa Ortiz
Sr. Customer Operations Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Jacqueline Hart <jacqueline.hart@acme-cloud.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Cloud Support <support@acme-cloud.com>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 10:02:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: EastUS3: Graceful warm-restart maintenance window (Aug 25, 2026)

Thanks for the heads up, Vanessa —

Quick question: our inference workers in EastUS3 host pools are running batch jobs that sometimes exceed 30m. Can you confirm whether queued batches will be resumed on the same host, or may be requeued to a different host? Also, can you flag any known customer-visible changes to model outputs after the kernel refresh?

Jacqueline
Platform Eng Lead, Acme Cloud

Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 12:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: EastUS3: Graceful warm-restart maintenance window (Aug 25, 2026)

Vanessa — forwarding Jacqueline's question. Two quick ops notes and a suggested change to external copy: 

1) Batching behavior: we will drain active batches gracefully; in-flight work should finish where possible. For queued batches not yet scheduled, scheduler may place them on alternate hosts if capacity requires it. Recommend we add a single sentence to the customer note: 'Queued batches may be migrated to other hosts; in-flight tasks will be allowed to complete when feasible.'

2) Output stability: the kernel refresh is minor; we are not changing model weights or runtime kernels that affect floating-point determinism. However, we will run a short smoke suite on a canary pool. Suggest we link the smoke-run report in the post-maintenance summary.

3) Communication tweak: customers with pinned/dedicated tenancy should appear in the first paragraph as 'We will minimize disruption to dedicated/pinned pools; contact us if you require an exception.'

Attaching the runbook for your visibility.

[attachment: eastus3-warm-restart-runbook.pdf]

- Aditya
Principal Site Reliability Engineer

Thanks Jacqueline — and thanks team. Short update based on Aditya's notes, and a final public copy below. We will: 

- Add the sentence about queued batches migrating when necessary.
- Add a line about dedicated/pinned pools and provide an exception request path (reply to thread).
- Run the smoke-suite on the canary pool 2 hours ahead of the window; results will post to the status link.

Final public copy (to be sent to customers and posted to Status):

Subject: EastUS3 maintenance (Aug 25) — graceful warm-restarts, minimal disruption expected\n
We will perform a coordinated warm-restart across host pools in EastUS3 on Tues Aug 25, 01:00–05:00 UTC. Queued batches may be migrated to other hosts; in-flight tasks will be allowed to complete when feasible. We will minimize disruption to dedicated/pinned pools — if you require an exception, reply to this message with your tenancy IDs by Fri Aug 21 EOD. A smoke-suite will run on canary hosts 2 hours prior; updates will be posted to https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/EUS3-2026-08-25.

We will send a post-maintenance summary with the smoke report and any follow-up actions.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Sr. Customer Operations Manager
Redwood Inference
